stem: The graph shows a cyclist speeding up steadily from 0 to 12 m/s in 8 seconds. Find the acceleration. The first steps are done.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 240 150" width="100%" style="max-width:240px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="Velocity-time graph. A straight line from 0 at 0 seconds up to 12 metres per second at 8 seconds">
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="220" y2="120" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="40" y2="15" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="180" y2="30" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <line x1="180" y1="30" x2="180" y2="120" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="30" x2="180" y2="30" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <text x="40" y="136" text-anchor="middle">0</text><text x="180" y="136" text-anchor="middle">8</text>
        <text x="34" y="124" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="34" y="34" text-anchor="end">12</text>
        <text x="130" y="148" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">time (s)</text>
        <text x="12" y="70" fill="#5f5f5a" transform="rotate(-90 12 70)" text-anchor="middle">m/s</text>
      </svg>
scaffold: Step 3: change in velocity 12 − 0 = 12 m/s. Time taken 8 s. Acceleration = 12 ÷ 8 = …
working: Step 3: change in velocity 12 − 0 = 12 m/s. Time taken 8 s. Acceleration = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 m/s².

misconceptions.message: You multiplied. Acceleration is change in velocity ÷ time.
You divided 8 by 12. The velocity change goes on top.
You subtracted 8 from 12. Divide, do not subtract.

stem: The graph shows a car speeding up steadily from 0 to 16 m/s in 10 seconds. Find the distance travelled. The first step is done.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 240 150" width="100%" style="max-width:240px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="Velocity-time graph. A straight line from 0 up to 16 metres per second at 10 seconds, with the triangle underneath shaded">
        <polygon points="40,120 190,120 190,25" fill="#e6f4ec"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="220" y2="120" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="40" y2="15" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="190" y2="25" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <line x1="190" y1="25" x2="190" y2="120" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <text x="40" y="136" text-anchor="middle">0</text><text x="190" y="136" text-anchor="middle">10</text>
        <text x="34" y="124" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="34" y="29" text-anchor="end">16</text>
        <text x="130" y="148" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">time (s)</text>
        <text x="12" y="70" fill="#5f5f5a" transform="rotate(-90 12 70)" text-anchor="middle">m/s</text>
      </svg>
scaffold: Step 5: the shape under the line is one triangle. Its base is 10 s. …
hint: The height of the triangle is the top speed. Then ½ × base × height.
working: Step 5: the shape under the line is one triangle. Its base is 10 s. Its height is 16 m/s. Step 6: ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 m.

misconceptions.message: You did base × height. A triangle is half of that.
You added 10 and 16. Area is ½ × base × height.
That is the acceleration, 16 ÷ 10. The question asks for distance, the area.

stem: On this graph, what is the velocity at 35 seconds?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" width="100%" style="max-width:300px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="Velocity-time graph rising from 0 to 20 metres per second at 10 seconds, flat to 30 seconds, then falling to 0 at 40 seconds. A dashed line marks 35 seconds">
        <line x1="40" y1="130" x2="280" y2="130" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="130" x2="40" y2="15" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <polyline points="40,130 95,30 205,30 260,130" fill="none" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <line x1="232" y1="130" x2="232" y2="80" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <text x="40" y="146" text-anchor="middle">0</text><text x="95" y="146" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="150" y="146" text-anchor="middle">20</text><text x="205" y="146" text-anchor="middle">30</text><text x="260" y="146" text-anchor="middle">40</text>
        <text x="232" y="158" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2b5797">35</text>
        <text x="34" y="134" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="34" y="84" text-anchor="end">10</text><text x="34" y="34" text-anchor="end">20</text>
        <text x="12" y="75" fill="#5f5f5a" transform="rotate(-90 12 75)" text-anchor="middle">m/s</text>
      </svg>
hint: Go up from 35 s to the red line, then across.
working: Between 30 s and 40 s the line drops steadily from 20 to 0. At 35 s it is halfway down: 10 m/s.

misconceptions.message: That is the top speed. At 35 s the line has dropped halfway.
That is at 40 s. At 35 s the car is still moving.
You read the time. Go up from 35 to the line, then across to the velocity axis.

stem: This is a distance-time graph of a walk. Find the speed in the first 20 seconds.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" width="100%" style="max-width:300px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="Distance-time graph. Distance in metres up the side. The line rises from 0 to 40 metres at 20 seconds, then stays flat at 40 until 30 seconds">
        <line x1="40" y1="130" x2="280" y2="130" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="130" x2="40" y2="15" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <polyline points="40,130 180,30 250,30" fill="none" stroke="#2e8b57" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <line x1="180" y1="30" x2="180" y2="130" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <text x="40" y="146" text-anchor="middle">0</text><text x="110" y="146" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="180" y="146" text-anchor="middle">20</text><text x="250" y="146" text-anchor="middle">30</text>
        <text x="160" y="158" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">time (s)</text>
        <text x="34" y="134" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="34" y="84" text-anchor="end">20</text><text x="34" y="34" text-anchor="end">40</text>
        <text x="12" y="75" fill="#5f5f5a" transform="rotate(-90 12 75)" text-anchor="middle">distance (m)</text>
      </svg>
hint: Read the side axis. It says distance, not velocity. How far in how long?
working: This is a distance-time graph, so the height is the distance and there is no area to find. 40 m in 20 s. Speed = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 m/s.

misconceptions.message: You found the area. On a distance-time graph the distance is the height, and speed is the gradient.
That is the distance. Speed is distance ÷ time: 40 ÷ 20.
You divided 20 by 40. Speed = distance ÷ time.

stem: A lift starts from rest and reaches 2 m/s after 4 seconds. It holds that speed for 6 seconds, then slows to a stop in 4 seconds. How many metres does it rise?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" width="100%" style="max-width:300px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="Velocity-time graph for the lift. Rises from 0 to 2 metres per second at 4 seconds, flat to 10 seconds, falls to 0 at 14 seconds. The area underneath is shaded">
        <polygon points="40,120 100,40 190,40 250,120" fill="#e6f4ec"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="280" y2="120" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <line x1="40" y1="120" x2="40" y2="15" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <polyline points="40,120 100,40 190,40 250,120" fill="none" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-width="2.5"/>
        <line x1="100" y1="40" x2="100" y2="120" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <line x1="190" y1="40" x2="190" y2="120" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <text x="40" y="136" text-anchor="middle">0</text><text x="100" y="136" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="190" y="136" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="250" y="136" text-anchor="middle">14</text>
        <text x="160" y="148" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">time (s)</text>
        <text x="34" y="124" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="34" y="44" text-anchor="end">2</text>
        <text x="12" y="70" fill="#5f5f5a" transform="rotate(-90 12 70)" text-anchor="middle">m/s</text>
      </svg>
hint: Split the shape: triangle, rectangle, triangle.
working: Triangle: ½ × 4 × 2 = 4. Rectangle: 6 × 2 = 12. Triangle: ½ × 4 × 2 = 4. Total: 4 + 12 + 4 = 20 m.

misconceptions.message: You did 2 × 14, one rectangle for the whole time. The two ends are triangles, half each.
That is only the middle rectangle, 6 × 2. Add the two triangles.
That is the top speed. Distance is the area.
